coordinates.note: ESTIMATED from video. Accuracy depends on the field registration — see the 'registration' block if present. These are not exact positions.
coordinates.units: yards; x downfield 0-120 with the offense attacking +x, y across 0-53.3

orientation.note: o is body orientation, dir is direction of travel; they are different and must not be derived from each other. o_source on every row says how that value was arrived at.

gaze.note: Where a player was LOOKING is not measured by anything, in this or any public football dataset. No such column exists here. The closest available signal is interactions.ball_in_view, which is inferred from body orientation and marked as inferred on every record.

reviewedPass.note: Carrier positions and interpolated airborne ground path are estimates, not ball detections.

ball.method: isolated brown object, camera-compensated sustained flight
ball.flight_projection: ground-plane projection of image sightings; altitude is not recovered
ball.note: A football in a wide broadcast shot is a few pixels and is behind somebody most of the play. Read measured_fraction AND travelled_yards before trusting any possession, passer or throw derived from this: a high detection rate on a static object is a confident wrong answer, and the generic sports-ball class finds broadcast graphics.

identity.method: checked full-formation anchor; fixed dormant identities
identity.note: Same-kit crossings/reacquisition are estimates; missing poses remain absent.

trackingQuality.identity: checked full-formation anchor; fixed dormant identities
notes: Same-kit crossings may switch identities; roster size does not establish identity accuracy.
Unobserved players are absent. Separation estimates may miss off-camera defenders.
Unidentified positions can cause linemen to be treated as possible receivers.
